decision.title: Each regex is compiled once per evaluation: the regex cache (packet )

item.p: Whom it serves: stylesheets and queries that call the regex functions in loops, above all SchXslt, whose expand stage calls fn:replace about 810,000 times with about 1,050 regex texts built from abstract patterns' parameter names. Each call parsed, compiled and placed its regex anew (compile_pattern).

Mechanism (glossary , src/function_library_regex.c): one cache per evaluation, keyed by the regex text and the parsed flags (so i and ii share an entry), used by fn:matches, fn:replace, fn:tokenize, fn:analyze-string, fn:matching-segments and fn:regex's functions alike. It lives where the dynamic context already keeps per-evaluation values: the evaluation memo (), as the state of a function item no expression can reach, made at the first regex call with a reference count (the parser function of fn:invisible-xml is the model). The memo releases it when the evaluation ends; each call using an entry holds a reference, so an fn:replace whose replacement function runs on the machine keeps its regex however the evaluation unwinds. The processor was not chosen: its lifetime and threads would need a lock and a header change, and one evaluation is where the repetition is. No field was added to the dynamic context, so src/evaluator.c (perf-5's) is unchanged. The lowering does not compile literal patterns: the cache gives the speed with one mechanism.

Bound and eviction: at most 4,096 entries and 8 MiB of compiled regexes with their texts (each entry is one block: the regex placed with sxml_regex_initialize, its text after it). A regex larger than 8 MiB is compiled for its call alone. A new entry evicts the least recently used entry that no call is using (a use clock and a scan: only a cache that is full scans); when every entry is in use the call compiles for itself. 4,096 covers SchXslt's 1,050 regexes used in a cycle, which a smaller least-recently-used cache would miss every time.

Limits: the memory comes from the item heap, so it counts against maximum_item_heap_byte_count. When an allocation for the cache reaches that limit (LIMIT_EXCEEDED), the unused entries are released and the allocation is tried once more, or the call compiles for itself, so the cache never makes a call reach the limit that would stay within it without the cache; other allocation failures are reported as before (the allocation-failure tests require it).

Errors and steps, per call: flags are parsed by every call (FORX0001); a regex that does not compile (FORX0002, or a compile limit) is never cached, so every call raises its error. Matchers are made per call as before (about 800 instructions), so the regex step limit and the steps charged to the evaluation are those of each search; compiling was never charged steps.

Measured (release, x86_64, processor seconds, fastest of five, before and after): 20,000 replace($s, "(\W*)\$AMOUNT(\W*)", "$1x$2") 0.103 to 0.065; with "\$AMOUNT" 0.050 to 0.031; tests/bench/regex-reuse.xq (new) 0.342 to 0.247; bench-real.xsl (39,000 fn:replace calls, 780 regexes) 0.550 to 0.488, at n=10 1.289 to 1.083 x 10^9 instructions, compile_pattern 20 % to 5 % of them (782 compiles for 23,400 calls); what is left is matching (the backtracking of (\W*) at every start position and sxml_regex_is_word_character's binary search). SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931 (step bound raised in a scratch build only): 555.5 to 550.9 s, the same output; compiling regexes was under 1 % of it, the rest is perf-5's problem. QT4 XP40 and XQ40 fn-analyze-string, fn-matches, fn-matches.re, fn-matching-segments, fn-regex, fn-replace, fn-tokenize, and XT40 analyze-string, regex, regex-syntax, regex-syntax-xslt20: 0 outcomes differ, case by case.
Left: an ASCII fast path for \w and \d (the generated src/regex_unicode.c); a matcher kept per entry would save its creation too, but holds a grown backtrack stack, so it is not done.
